name: National Gallery
description: The national collection of European painting from the 1200s to 1900, on the north side of Trafalgar Square. Entry is free.

name: Trafalgar Square
description: The big public square with Nelson’s Column, fountains and bronze lions, and the old official measures of length set into its steps.

name: British Museum
description: A huge free museum of world history and culture in Bloomsbury, with the Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies and the Parthenon sculptures.

name: Tate Britain
description: The national gallery of British art from 1500 to today, on the river at Millbank, with a large collection of Turner. Entry is free.

name: Courtauld Gallery
description: A small gallery in Somerset House with a fine collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings, plus Old Masters.

name: Monument to the Great Fire
places: Monument to the Great Fire of London
description: A stone column near where the Great Fire of 1666 began. You can climb its 311 steps to a viewing platform.

name: Palace of Westminster
description: The riverside home of the Houses of Parliament, rebuilt in Gothic style after a fire in 1834, with the clock tower that holds Big Ben.

name: Parliament Square
description: A green square between Parliament and Westminster Abbey, ringed with statues of statesmen and a frequent site of protests.

name: St Paul’s Cathedral
description: The domed cathedral rebuilt after the Great Fire of 1666, with galleries up in the dome and crypts below.

name: Tate Modern
description: The national gallery of modern and contemporary art, in a former power station on the South Bank. Entry to the collection is free.

name: Tower of London
places: Yeoman Warders’ Club, Tower of London
description: The medieval fortress on the Thames, once a royal palace and prison, now home to the Crown Jewels and the Yeoman Warders.

name: Covent Garden Market
description: The old fruit and vegetable market hall in the West End, now shops, stalls and cafés, with street performers in the piazza.

name: John Snow pump
description: A replica water pump in Soho marking where, in 1854, a doctor traced a cholera outbreak to a contaminated well.

name: 430 King’s Road
description: The Chelsea shop where Malcolm McLaren and Vivienne Westwood sold clothes in the 1970s, at the centre of the early punk scene.

name: Gay’s the Word
description: Britain’s oldest LGBT bookshop, open in Bloomsbury since 1979.

name: Shakespeare’s Globe
description: A reconstruction of Shakespeare’s open-air playhouse on the South Bank, opened in 1997, where plays are staged much as they were around 1600.

name: Roman wall at Tower Hill
description: One of the best-surviving stretches of the Roman wall that once enclosed London, beside Tower Hill station.

name: Royal Albert Hall
description: The round, domed concert hall in South Kensington, opened in 1871, home every summer to the Proms.

name: Buckingham Palace
description: The monarch’s London home and office, at the end of the Mall. The state rooms open to visitors in summer.

name: British Library
description: The national library of the UK, in a red-brick building next to St Pancras, with a free gallery of manuscripts such as Magna Carta.

name: Beigel Bake
description: A bagel bakery on Brick Lane, open 24 hours, known for its salt beef bagels.

name: Victoria and Albert Museum
places: Cast Courts, Victoria and Albert Museum
description: A huge free museum of art and design in South Kensington, including the Cast Courts, halls of plaster copies of famous sculpture and buildings.

name: Thames Barrier
description: A row of steel flood gates across the Thames at Woolwich, in use since 1982 to protect London from tidal surges.

name: Dulwich Picture Gallery
description: England’s oldest public art gallery, opened in 1817 in south London, with a collection of Old Master paintings.

name: Westminster Abbey
places: Henry VII Lady Chapel, Westminster Abbey
description: The Gothic abbey church where English and British monarchs are crowned, and many are buried, including in the fan-vaulted Lady Chapel.

name: London Mithraeum
places: London Mithraeum (Temple of Mithras), Bloomberg building
description: The remains of a Roman temple to the god Mithras, shown in the basement of the Bloomberg building in the City. Entry is free.
